_comment: Hike stats from Grok research 2026-08-19 (reference/grok-handoff-hikes.md).
UNITS TRAP: AllTrails quotes ROUND TRIP; NPS/FS trail tables quote ONE WAY.
Karl's stated preference is 1.5-4.0 mi EACH WAY. Every entry therefore
carries both raw figures AND a computed each_way_mi so nothing is compared
across different units.
Where sources DISAGREE, both are kept and both are cited. None is averaged
into a single confident number -- the disagreement is information about how
well the distance is actually known.
Claude's own OSM foot-routing figure is stored alongside as a third
independent measure. For Lake Isabelle: OSM 2.4, FS 2.0, AllTrails 3.3 mi
each way. Agreement across three methods is why any of them can be printed.
Dogs and permits are LABELS. An RMNP lake stays on the list with its ban
shown; it is never hidden.

2026-08-28: the AllTrails CONNECTOR went live in Claude Code, so figures below tagged source 'alltrails-connector' came from the API directly rather than from Grok reading pages. That also unlocked review summaries and ratings, which the page-reading pass could not get (JavaScript-rendered).

_comment: Dog and permit rules, keyed by LAND MANAGER, because that is what actually
determines them. Every entry carries the source it came from and the date it
was fetched. Nothing here is recalled at runtime -- a sheet prints the rule
AND its citation so Karl can check it himself when he is somewhere with no
signal and a ranger is telling him otherwise.
Re-fetch before each trip: these change between seasons.

National Park Service.detail: Pets are prohibited on ALL trails, tundra and meadows. Leashed pets (max 6 ft) are allowed only along established roads, in parking areas, and in established campgrounds and picnic areas. Pets may NOT be left unattended in vehicles.

United States Forest Service.detail: Leashed dogs are allowed on most Forest Service trails. Some areas have their own rules -- Brainard Lake differs by season -- so check the specific trail.

Boulder County Open Space.detail: Leashed and under physical control on properties where dogs are allowed. Four properties prohibit dogs entirely -- see named_exceptions.

Bureau of Land Management.detail: Varies by field office and by area. Not established for this trip.

named_exceptions.detail: Dogs are not permitted at Caribou Ranch Open Space at all. It is immediately next to Nederland, which makes it an easy place to drive to and be turned away from.

permits.name: RMNP timed entry

windows.label: Rest of park (excludes Bear Lake Road)

permits.free_windows: No permit is required outside those hours -- before 09:00 or after 14:00 for the rest of the park, and before 05:00 or after 18:00 for the Bear Lake corridor.
permits.release: Reservations open on Recreation.gov at 08:00 MDT one month ahead: Aug 1 for September dates, Sep 1 for Oct 1-18. A further 40% of each day is released at 19:00 MDT the evening before.

access_areas.name: Brainard Lake Recreation Area
access_areas.why_it_matters: Gates every Indian Peaks lake near Nederland - Isabelle, Mitchell, Blue, Long. Same class of avoidable failure as the Caribou Ranch dog ban.

timed_entry.required_for: Driving in and parking inside the recreation area. Sold ONLY on Recreation.gov, never on-site.
timed_entry.trip_dates_status: Oct 2-5 falls AFTER the published ticket season. The official pages do NOT say driving in is free after Oct 1 - they say the gate runs mid-June to mid-October, closing weather-dependent. Treat access as UNCONFIRMED and check Boulder Ranger District road status the week before.
timed_entry.long_lake_note: Long Lake Trailhead is its own separate ticket, 30 cars, park in the lot named on the reservation.

fallback.name: Gateway Trailhead
fallback.detail: Year-round, NO timed entry, but 2 miles from Brainard Lake. If the gate is shut this is where you park - and it adds about 2 miles EACH WAY to every lake beyond it.
fallback.fees: Summer day use free; winter (mid-Oct to mid-June) $10 at Gateway.

access_areas.fees: $16 personal vehicle / $9 motorcycle / $38 van. Pass holders still buy the reservation; Recreation.gov charges $2 processing.
access_areas.shuttle: Gateway to Brainard Lake TH, $5 round trip, generally Fri-Sun 8-6. NO PETS - useless on a day the dogs come.
access_areas.dogs: Hand-held leash May 1 - Nov 14 in the recreation area and at Long Lake; the Mitchell Lake page words it May 1 - Nov 1. Oct 2-5 sits inside BOTH, so dogs are fine on Isabelle, Mitchell and Blue. Winter roads-only rule does not start until Nov 15.

_comment: What each subject is actually DOING during the trip window, and what that
means for the chance of an interesting frame rather than a portrait.
Sourced and dated. Karl named 'action -- flight, hunting, rut' as one of the
three things that make a shot great, so this decides real points and must
not be recalled at runtime.
Re-check before any trip in a different season: every entry here is seasonal.

elk.detail: Rut. Elk descend from the high country to montane meadows for the autumn breeding season, and are most active morning and evening. Bugling and sparring are the frame worth having.
elk.restriction: During the rut, RMNP meadow areas prohibit foot travel off established roadways and designated trails from 17:00 to 10:00 daily. Evening elk work is roadside by regulation. Keep 75 ft (two bus lengths) minimum.

bighorn.detail: NOT in rut during this trip. Bighorn breed in November and December, peaking in early December, so rams will be solitary or in bachelor groups rather than clashing. Rams are present and photographable; the head-butting is six to eight weeks after Karl goes home.

raptors.detail: Soaring on thermals is flight, not a perch -- the behaviour is the shot. Thermals need a few hours of sun on the ground, so this is a mid-morning to mid-afternoon subject.
raptors.source: engine/sun.py thermal_window; threshold is a rule of thumb, not validated against observation data

owls.detail: Hunting begins at dusk, but most keeper frames are a perched bird in very low light. Action is possible rather than likely, and it is the hardest exposure on the trip.

landscape.detail: Static subject. Light is the whole game, so this scores on the light term and nothing else.

fall-color.detail: Static, and additionally dependent on this year's timing, which moves with summer moisture and must be checked against current reports near the date.

model.rule: Colour descends ~1.5 days per 100 m of elevation.
model.status: MODEL, not observation. The same page's county forecast (Larimer and Boulder, Sep 17-21) disagrees with this rule at low elevation. Show both.

sources.what: Interactive map with a date slider; states that it updates daily against real-time weather.

provenance.sun/moon: engine/sun.py, engine/moon.py — NOAA and truncated ELP2000-82, offline. Verified against api.sunrise-sunset.org (48/48) and USNO (45/45), each with a mutation that must be caught.
provenance.drive times: OSRM public router. Never estimated from straight-line distance.
provenance.elevation: USGS EPQS 1 m raster, Open-Elevation fallback.
provenance.birds: eBird API 2.0, PUBLIC HOTSPOTS ONLY. Personal locations are somebody's house and are filtered out.
provenance.mammals: iNaturalist research-grade, DATE-FILTERED. A recency-limited query missed 95 September elk and reported zero.
provenance.jurisdiction: OpenStreetMap via Overpass is_in, mirrored with a coverage canary — a regional mirror answers an out-of-area query with an empty result, not an error.
provenance.trails: AllTrails connector (live) plus agency pages. Where they disagree BOTH figures are kept.
provenance.rules: NPS, US Forest Service, Boulder County — each entry dated.
